title: Sidney Cate, the Moonlight Serenaders and Son Johnson
summary: Son Johnson played with Sidney Cate's Moonlight Serenaders and a WPA band at Lemon Playground; local musicians rarely left home.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Oh he plays clarinet too. I can't think. Well did you meet Son Johnson in New Orleans? I can't think.
Very, he played alto saxophone and he played clarinet too. I can't think. Well he played, let's see, he was playing with the Moonlight Serenaders.

You ever run into the fellas with the Moonlight Serenaders down there? No. No. What was this fella, big tall, like fella, he was a guitar player. He was in charge. I think at one time he was president of the local down there.
I don't know who that was. Now Louis Cottrell is president.
Well Cottrell is recent. Because Cottrell used to play with Don Albert, right? Yeah. But Sidney Cate. Oh yeah. Remember Sidney Cate?

Yeah, well Sidney Cate used to be in charge of the union at one particular time. He's secretary now. Yeah. Well he had a band, they called themselves the Moonlight Serenaders. And during the time when I was playing with this young group I had mentioned about earlier the program about the group that was comprised of fellows from school. Well anyhow, Son Johnson was playing with him. And I remember quite a bit about Son because of the fact that he also played with this WPA band that was organized in 19, just after Prohibition. Yeah, they used to play in the park there, at the playground, every Wednesday or Thursday. And we used to make special efforts, you know, to get down there and listen to the music. We'd play a while. Which park was that? It was Lemon Playground, right on Basin Street. You know where Basin Street? Yeah. Right there. Well it's called Lafitte Street. Oh yeah, sure I know. It's Lafitte Street. That's right. And it was just after this new playground had been inaugurated, this Lemon Playground, and then they'd start having his bands come out there. And well if you looked at the fellow you would never think he could play a note. You know he looked so unconcerned about everything and dressed casual and he had several opportunities to go with various bands out east and he never went and I understand that he had gone someplace for a while and he got tired after about a week and a half and came back home. I mean the same thing goes true for a fellow like even Pernell, Theodore Pernell. He's had several opportunities. But I know for some particular reason the fellows never wanted to leave home.
